audits.the_argument: Two-part record. The ORIGINAL arm (turn_far_thinning = far-ladder change reads the running turn) was tested on the S95 fingerprint pass and DEMOTED to noise - a real falsification, executed, recorded, and the play rewritten around it. I reproduced that demotion off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json: across all 6,358 committed legs, legs that CONTINUED carry a 37.4% negative-turn_far_thinning share and legs that FADED carry 30.7%. A 6.7-point separation on n=6,358 is not a discriminator, and the sign of the difference runs AGAINST the arm's original direction (the turning legs are the LESS far-thinned ones). The demotion was correct and if anything understated. The SURVIVING arm (old-swing continuation-collapse + negative turn_exhaustion + peaked_fast) rests on one named instance, 1008 old-swing up-legs 0/15, which reproduces EXACTLY: 20251008 carries 15 up legs and 0 continued, against 12 of 26 down legs continuing on the same day. That is an argued mechanism (the old swing stops recruiting before price turns) with a traced first instance, which is NOVEL_N1 by the rubric's own discriminator - not ASSERTED. What it is NOT is MECHANISM_VERIFIED: there is no base rate, no non-turn control day, and no measured hit-rate for the surviving arm on its own. The record itself scopes it further - the surviving measurement is the SAME quantity as chain_polarity_flip C2 and inherits C2's G11 false negative and the S100.3 finding that it is non-discriminating on the 0107/0120 tape class.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, decisively, for the demoted arm - it was tested and it failed, and the play was rewritten to say so. That is the strongest single signal in this batch that the desk's measurements are real. NO for the surviving arm as currently supported: 0/15 is a striking number but it is one hand-picked turn day with no control, so nothing in the present evidence could have refuted the continuation-collapse read. The base rate that would settle it is computable from the same committed file and has never been computed.

audits.the_argument: The claim is: at a block boundary, lean AGAINST a stretched swing when the running path is at a cum-extreme AND the old swing shows a counter-move in its last 1-2 days AND last-hour momentum rolls over. The support is 'n=5 turns across 4 blocks' plus a per-event chronology - and the chronology is a list of days SELECTED BECAUSE THEY TURNED, with the mechanism rewritten after each block to fit what happened: after G6 it became 'a GIVE-BACK, not a sustained reversal'; after G7 'the give-back can be one day deep'; the caveats field then records five successive reframes and ends by conceding the play has been SUPERSEDED as a block-lean caller and 'is retained as the historical record of the seam lean'. That is the reframe-to-fit signature, and no amount of arithmetic accuracy cures it. || AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ACCURATE - I checked all of it. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/g3g4g5_rt.json: 0925 +740, 0929 +950, 1001 +1170, 1008 -1800, 0923 +610, 0924 +50, 0922 cum -2250 (the G3 extreme) - every figure exact. The '1019 +1570 overnight gap' is exact as a GAP (net that session was -50), so the play is quoting the right field. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/g7_rt.json the entire G7 forward arm is exact to the dollar: 1113 cum +2810 with an intraday peak +1160 closing +620 (the last-hour roll-over), 1114 -910, 1117 -1500, 1118 +270 stabilization, retrace -2590. Two figures I could NOT reproduce ('1007 +2120 roll-clean' vs the unadjusted +1360; '1016 -3770 roll-clean' vs -1100) are cited as roll-clean and the rt line declares itself NOT roll-adjusted, so that is a basis difference, not an error - I am not scoring it against the play. || WHAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING WORSE than OUTCOME_CREDITED is one genuine arming discipline: in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp7_seq_experiment.json the trigger sat HALF-lit at a cum-extreme (1104 up-legs healthy, no continuation-collapse) and the run DECLINED to fade - and the record shows the trigger then stayed half-armed through the block's later extremes until 1113. A trigger that visibly refuses to fire is doing real work. But it is one instance and the play no longer owns the decision.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the n=5 evidence base - those five turns are the definition of the sample, so the mechanism cannot fail on them. PARTIALLY YES for G7: the arming sequence (half-armed at earlier extremes, fully armed 1113, delivered 1114/1117, stopped at the origin shelf 1118) was a forward test with a stated arming rule that could have fired early and did not, and could have run past the shelf and did not. And the play carries a recorded MISS in its own text (G6 week-2 recovery), which is more honesty than most. One forward confirmation plus one recorded miss is not a measurement base for a block-lean caller.

audits.the_argument: Claim: in a running chain, a counter-chain intraday spike that ROUND-TRIPS (closes >=~60% off the counter extreme), especially on the best remaining counter-catalyst, means counter-side liquidity is exhausted and the next session runs hard chain-side. This is the only play in my batch whose arming quantity and whose consequence are BOTH independently measured and BOTH reproduce exactly. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/: 20251210 intraday peak +1060 closing +370 (65% off) -> 20251211 -3970; 20251230 peak +1990 closing +180 (91% off) -> 20251231 -2630; 20251002 peak +900 closing -440 -> 20251003 -680; 20260113 peak +1190 closing +320 (73% off) -> 20260114 -2710. Four for four, exact to the dollar, spanning G4, G9 and G10. The arming input (the fade percentage) is computed from the realized curve and is NOT the thing being predicted; the consequence (next-day net) could have been any number. That is the definition of evidence that could have come out otherwise. || I ADDED A BASE RATE, because four selected pairs are still four selected pairs. Across every committed rt file I defined the arming condition mechanically - an up-spike of >=$500 that round-tripped >=60% and still closed positive - and got n=9, of which 6 delivered a DOWN next day, against an unconditional down-day base rate of 93/171 = 54%. 67% vs 54% on n=9 is weak on its own. But the three FAILURES are 20250908 (+120 next), 20250915 (+1200) and 20251006 (+1360), and all three sit inside UP swings - which is exactly the polarity condition the play requires and my mechanical screen ignored. Conditioned on the play's own down-chain polarity the record is 6 of 6. The play's own G11 note independently reaches the same conclusion from the other direction: the two G11 misses (0121, 0127) were fired against give-backs inside an UP chain, and the record says in terms 'the tell has never been tested at up-polarity'. Two roads to the same scope boundary. || THE RECORD ALSO CARRIES ITS COUNTER-EVIDENCE, which is why this is not OUTCOME_CREDITED: G11 scored 2/4 and the brain wrote the loss down and cut confidence 0.5 -> 0.45; and in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp21_mbo_specialist_A.json the refine specialist tells the merge in writing 'Do not bank 0619 as forward evidence for structure.failed_rally_tell' after its own blind route was refuted on the correct leg. That is the S108 disease being caught at the merge boundary by the specialist that would have benefited - the opposite of the defect this audit hunts.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, and it did, repeatedly. The four founding pairs each have an independently-measured arming quantity and an unconstrained consequence. G11 gave it four forward fires and it went 2/4, and the record kept the loss instead of re-scoping it away. G21 produced an explicit do-not-bank instruction from the specialist that armed it. My own mechanical screen produced three failures and they turned out to name the play's known polarity boundary rather than break it.

audits.condition_can_change_state: YES on the refine side and the split is real: my mechanical screen found 9 qualifying round-trips across ~171 committed sessions, so roughly 5% of days arm it - a discriminating bar, not a degenerate one. NO on the blind side, and this is the usability defect that matters. The arming quantity is the D-1 intraday spike/fade percentage, which is price content. The brain's own g11_note states it: 'All four ran without day-N-1 actual tape, so the spike-fade percentage that arms the tell was assumed from the GUESSED CURVE rather than observed.' A condition computed from the forecaster's own drawing cannot come out the other way - it will agree with whatever curve was drawn. In blind mode this play does not have an input; it has a mirror. G20 and G21 both solved that by declaring a FLOW substitute, which is the right instinct, but the substitute is a different quantity and has never been scored as one.

If the flow analogue does not track the price analogue, the blind's version of this play is a different play wearing its name.

audits.the_argument: A gap-ownership rung with a four-limb conjunction: (a) BOTH futures books at 1y short extremes (NYMEX MM pctile <=~12 AND ICE LD1 <=~3) with a climax add or first covering print, (b) price at/near the bleed low, (c) a bullish storage-trajectory catalyst, (d) THE WINDOW - curve_regime contango while storage phase is withdraw. Mechanism argued and physical: a saturated short book at the lows facing a storage catalyst has no marginal seller, and a headroom-bounded warm cut cannot refill it. || THE EVIDENCE IS A BACK-CHECK, WHICH IS THE RIGHT SHAPE - a 15-gap sweep of every walk anchor with ZERO false fires, naming for each anchor WHICH limb failed. That could have produced false fires and did not. I tested the structural core of it myself against the committed states: across ALL 192 day-rows in every grp*_state.json in the repo, limb (d) is true on exactly four - 20260301, 20260302, 20260308, 20260309, all in G14 - and 0301/0308 are the only Sunday/Monday ANCHORS anywhere in the corpus where it holds. The play's claim that these are its unique qualifying anchors is corroborated independently. The two gaps reproduce exactly off g14_rt.json: 0301 gap +720, 0308 gap +1220. || THE FORWARD RECORD IS DECLINES, AND THEY ARE GOOD ONES. G15 declined twice with named numbers (0313->0315: NYMEX 25.5/ICE 10.4 and backwardation; 0320->0322: phase flipped to injection at the 0319 print, NYMEX 50.0 despite ICE 2.83). G20/G22/G23 keep declining with the same discipline - G22 specialist B and D each write out which limb failed and by how much, D noting 'One of two is not the conjunction'. Six groups, zero mis-ownership. || THE HAIRLINE, and it is the only thing wrong with this play. Limb (a)'s NYMEX bar is written '<=~12'. Both supporting instances read 12.26. Under a strict <=12 the play's own two founding gaps FAIL its own bar, and they are admitted only by the tilde. A bar sited at the exact edge of its own support is fitted to its support - the mirror image of the D23 finding that the healthiest bars sit at the CENTRE of their distribution. It has cost nothing so far because limb (d) has gated everything anyway, but it is a latent value-keyed condition of exactly the kind D23 was opened to catch.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, twice over. The 15-gap back-check is a genuine falsification opportunity - any anchor passing all four limbs and NOT delivering a counter-side gap would have refuted it, and the sweep names each failing limb rather than asserting a clean result. And the forward record is DECLINES with served numbers, which is the hardest kind of evidence to fake: a play that declines correctly when its limbs fail is being run honestly. My independent recomputation of limb (d) across 192 day-rows could have contradicted the 'only 0301/0308' claim and did not.

audits.condition_can_change_state: SPLIT ANSWER, and both halves matter. Limb (a) DOES change state and discriminates well: BOTH-books-at-extremes is true on 10 of 60 day-rows in G17-G23 (all of G18) and false elsewhere - a healthy split. Limb (d) is 0 of 60 in G17-G23 and 0 of 192 across every committed state file OUTSIDE G14, because the walk since G16 has been entirely in the injection phase. So the CONJUNCTION is 0-of-192 outside its founding block: the play has had no opportunity to fire, correctly or otherwise, since G14. This is honestly declared ('Mid-winter extremes excluded by (d) by design') and is a seasonal-window property rather than a defect - but it means six groups of 'zero false fires' is a weaker forward statement than it reads, since the gate that produced most of those declines was a calendar, not a market read. Separately: the 12.26-vs-'<=~12' hairline on limb (a) means the play's two founding instances sit outside a strict reading of its own bar.
audits.falsifier: Brain falsifier field is EMPTY, but the play carries a de facto one in its back-check design: any anchor passing (a)+(b)+(c)+(d) whose gap does NOT price to the counter/covering side refutes it, and the sweep was built to look for exactly that. The addition I would make: state limb (a) in SHAPE form (per D23) - both books in their own bottom decile, or a stated distance from each book's own 1y distribution - rather than as absolute percentile bars, one of which currently sits 0.26 points inside its own instances. And the play cannot be forward-tested at all until the walk re-enters a withdraw-phase contango window; that is a scheduling fact the plant should record, not an open question.

audits.the_argument: Claim: in a confirmed S1-void spring injection block under a sub-0.50 sell tape, do NOT damp a chain-sided down day to a stub - a TREND day delivers -450..-780 and a COIL day -100..-250. The mechanism is argued and is not silly (S1-void removes the seasonal amplifier but not the storage-trajectory lean; a live sell tape means a live chain; the G15 do-not-over-size lesson was mis-transferred from counter days to chain days). But the SUPPORT is eleven G16 days listed WITH their realized moves - 0329 -790, 0330 -650, 0401 -600, 0406 -470, 0408 -450, 0409 -610 for the trend band; 0331 -110, 0402 -130, 0407 -220, 0410 -190 for the coil band - and the bands are the range of those realized moves. The DISCRIMINATOR (which band applies) is a day-class label assigned to the same days whose moves define the bands. It calls it WITHOUT a book read. || THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED AT THE RIGHT GRAIN AND HAS BEEN RECONFIRMED THREE TIMES IN THREE DIFFERENT GROUPS - this is the strongest thing in the play and it is genuine. G15 founding pair, verbatim from the source posterior: 0316 inherited age 1, ph2 late buy +959 ACCOMMODATED, close_off_low 0.29, day -540 (posterior -570, err -30); 0323 inherited age 3 with cum -890, ph2 buy +2409 ABSORBED (price still fell), close_off_low 0.14, day -1080 (posterior -1080, err 0). The evidence field reads 'All three self-analyses (C/D/E S105) independently prescribed a mid-block re-derivation' - three agents agreeing on a prescription is convergence, not evidence, and none of them could have been refuted by it. The diagnostic number quoted ('~70% of misses across C/D/E were signals SEEN and not acted on') is a retrospective attribution of misses to a cause the play was written to name. || AND THE FORWARD FIELD CARRIES THE S108 SIGNATURE IN ONE SENTENCE: 'G17 refine r2: the HE24->HE1 coordination halved error 24->11 (10/10) WITH ZERO DIRECTION CHANGES - the mid-block re-derivation working.' This play's entire action is a SIGN CHANGE. A run with zero direction changes is a run in which the play's signature is absent, and a magnitude improvement on such a run cannot be attributed to it. Right answer, credited to a mechanism that provably did not fire - the exact pattern that forced the s103.6 retraction. || I SCORED THE ACTUAL FIRES. Blind unlocks: G18 0506 emitted +100, actual -530 (wrong); G21 0616 emitted +180, actual +970 (right); G21 0617 'the stack has now built across four sessions' emitted +110, actual -970 (wrong); G21 0618 emitted +950, actual +520 (right). audits.the_argument: A consistency constraint, not a market conditional: a chain's polarity and age must DERIVE from the realized cum carried in the handoff, no day may open with a chain label contradicting the inherited cum, no day restarts at cum 0, and a specialist that cannot state the inherited cum and the prior close's range-location may not assert a chain polarity at all. Confidence 0.88 - the highest in my batch. || THE MECHANISM IS ARGUED AND THE FIRST INSTANCE IS FULLY TRACED, which is NOVEL_N1 exactly. G19 ran with every blind day reset to cum 0; B then wrote an 'age-5 DOWN chain' against a realized five-session UP covering rally. Both halves are in the corpus: the label itself in research/kalshi/forecasts/g19_blind_round1/grp19_mbo_specialist_B.json ('inherited chain age 5 (mature, >=3)'), and its refutation in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp19_postmortem_B.json ('The age-5 DOWN chain was fiction: the realized chain was a five-session UP covering rally (2.750 -> 3.019 open)... Starting each Monday fresh at cum 0 with no inheritance is exactly what let me invent a down chain against a week of realized up days'). Blind -550, actual +660, miss -1210. The inherited cum at 0515 close was +2110 (g19_actual.json), so the contradiction is arithmetic, not interpretive. The brain's 'corroborated by all five post-mortems' is prose citing prose - per the instance-discipline rule that is ONE instance, not five. || THE PLAY HAS CHANGED BEHAVIOUR, VISIBLY AND WIDELY, which is more than most process rules achieve. Every G22 blind specialist and both G23 owners I read now DECLARE the basis of their chain label rather than asserting one. A-0703 is the model: 'DOWN, age 5 at the close, FLOW-DERIVED. MANDATORY WARNING per boundary.chain_label_must_track_realized_cum: this label has NO realized cum behind it... The moment the next owner sees realized cum, RE-DERIVE and OVERRULE me.' 0703 then delivered +410 against A's -160 - the label WAS wrong, and the rule had already flagged it. || AND THE PLAY CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE ONE POINT IT IS MOST EMPHATIC ABOUT. Its caveat says 'The masked-price case is NOT an exemption: chain STATE travels in the handoff, which is never masked.' That is false on the served state, and seven posteriors say so: E-0626 'boundary.chain_label_must_track_realized_cum requires REALIZED cum, which is price-masked'; B-0629 'price cum declared unknowable rather than invented' (substituting cumulative signed flow, -3,909 lots); E-0710 'flow-derived substitute; requires realized cum, which is masked'; B-0713 'cum masked + staleness-gated'. What survives, and is arguably the better rule, is DECLARE-YOUR-BASIS-AND-FLAG-IT-FOR-OVERRIDE. That is not what the entry says.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES for the founding instance - the label could have been consistent with the inherited cum and was not, and the arithmetic gap (a five-session UP cum of +2110 labelled an age-5 DOWN chain) is unarguable. PARTIALLY for the forward record: compliance is observable and near-universal on G22/G23, and A-0703 is a case where the rule's own warning was borne out. What has NOT been shown is that enforcement improves accuracy - the postmortem's 'the handoff would have flipped 0518 to UP' is a counterfactual, not a measurement, and no scored comparison of enforced vs unenforced runs exists.

audits.condition_can_change_state: Not a numeric bar - it is a consistency constraint, so the question becomes: is it EVALUABLE? Only partly, and this is the finding. Realized cum_from_anchor is price content and IS masked in the blind, so on the modern architecture the rule's own required input is absent for the runs that need it most. It IS available in the handoff files (forecasts/g*_he24_he1_handoffs.json carry chain_polarity, chain_age_sessions and cum_from_anchor_usd) for in-block boundaries, and it IS available to the refine. So the rule is fully evaluable on refine runs and in-block refine boundaries, partly evaluable on in-block blind days (flow-cum substitute, declared), and NOT evaluable at all on block-open days (0622, 0608: no prior-group handoff exists). The compliance rate is what actually changed: near-universal declaration across G22/G23 versus zero inheritance in G19.

Also worth building: serve chain age/polarity as a computed state field, which would simultaneously fix monday.seam_chainage_accommodation_gate's input problem.

If it steps hard against your thesis, say so and widen, rather than resolving it in your own favour.' audits.the_argument: Claim: on a day whose D-1 carried a scheduled program (expiry, BCOM/GSCI roll, opex), the next-day gate must consume the PROGRAM-DECONTAMINATED residual tilt, and the receiving specialist reads it IN PLACE OF session_signed_flow's sign. || THE CONTAMINATION MECHANISM IS REAL AND WAS VERIFIED PRICE-FREE, which I want to credit clearly. B-0629 established it three independent ways without touching price: flow_calendar.is_expiry_day TRUE on 0626 (NGN26's expiry) with the scored leg the deferred NGQ26, so every roll and expiring-long transfer prints as an aggressor BUY on the measured leg; and 'THE DISPOSITIVE ONE: session_signed_flow FELL from +1,956 on 0625 to +871 on 0626 on the day big_print_b_share supposedly flipped from 0.499 to 0.783. Less aggregate net buying on the day the blocks turned buy.' That forces the residual non-block tape to be a net seller. Sound, and it is a genuine measurement. || BUT THE PLAY IS NOT THE CONTAMINATION, IT IS THE SIGN SUBSTITUTION - and the support for THAT is one day that came out right. Evidence field: 'B-0629: the tilt gate fed +871 gross and weighted the self-derived residual 0.10 - the sign correction in r1 was the blind's own rule fed a decontaminated input.' Blind emitted +325, actual -1,110, refine emitted -1,000. One day, and the mechanism promoted from it. || AND THE COUNTER-INSTANCE IS ALREADY IN THE RECORD, FROM THE SPECIALIST THAT PROPOSED THE PLAY. On 0710 the residual read INVERTED - big-print 0.550 BUY against a -1,225 SELL aggregate - and B consumed it on E's written instruction. B's own refine: 'REJECTED - THE BIG-PRINT RESIDUAL AS THE D-1 TILT SUBSTITUTE, and with it my own use of handoff.residual_tilt_field as a sign channel... The discarded field is the one that matched Monday.' Blind +550, actual -620. So n=2 and the two point OPPOSITE ways: 1-1. || THE RECORD DOES NOT ACT ON ITS OWN COUNTER-INSTANCE. status is still PROPOSED, forward_evidence still reads 'n=2 spanning', and the CALL still says the receiving specialist reads the residual 'in place of session_signed_flow's sign' - the precise instruction that produced the wrong Monday. The inversion is recorded in a legacy note; the operative text is unchanged. || TWO THINGS I CHECKED THAT SHARPEN IT. (1) I reproduced the corpus rate independently: D-1 aggregate flow sign predicts next-day sign 26 of 59 = 44% across G18-G23 (per group 6/10, 4/10, 3/10, 6/10, 4/9, 3/10). The thing being replaced is a coin flip, so the bar for the replacement is low and it has not cleared it. (2) The scope claims 'n=2 (G21 0616, G22 0629)', but 0616's D-1 (0615) is not a program day at all - flow_calendar shows days_to_futures_expiry 7, days_to_opex 6, no roll day number - and the G21 contamination was the S108 hole-#8 truncated/off-instrument capture (grp21_mbo_specialist_C.json: tc_sflow -624 vs mbo_sflow -5,687, '9.1x UNDERSTATED and SHAPE-INVERTED'). That is a DATA defect, not a program cohort. The stated n=2 conflates two different contamination mechanisms and the play's program-day scope does not cover one of them.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: For the CONTAMINATION claim, yes - B-0629 built a price-free falsifiable argument (aggregate flow falling on the day the blocks turned buy is not something a clean tape does) and it could have failed. For the SUBSTITUTION RULE, which is what the play actually instructs, the founding evidence is a single day that delivered the residual's side - and when it was given a genuine forward test on 0713 it produced the wrong sign and its own author withdrew it. The evidence for the rule is 1-1 on n=2 against a 44% baseline, which is no evidence at all.

audits.condition_can_change_state: The TRIGGER can (program days are a genuine minority - flow_calendar serves is_expiry_day, in_gsci_roll, in_bcom_roll, is_opex_day, and specialists correctly declare the contrapositive on non-program days, e.g. C-0708 'D-1 carried NO program (verified in_gsci_roll false 0707), so the raw +1748 aggregate is the clean tilt'). But THE READ CANNOT BE COMPUTED: the play's stated input is a big-print cohort decomposition of the D-1 tape and tape_conditions serves no cohort decomposition, which C states twice in G23. So on the days it fires, the field is constructed by hand as a declared proxy rather than measured - and it is precisely on program-heavy weeks (4 of 5 usable G23 reads) that this bites. Worse for the sign claim: the aggregate it replaces predicts next-day sign 26/59 = 44% (I reproduced this), so the incumbent is a coin flip and the replacement's own record is 1-1.
audits.falsifier: The brain DOES carry one here, and it is well posed: 'a program day whose residual tilt misleads while the gross aggregate reads true.' THAT DAY HAS OCCURRED - 0713 is exactly it, and it is recorded in the play's own legacy note - yet status remains PROPOSED and the call text is unchanged. Per D31 the refutation is scoped to the cell it was measured on and does not kill the play; but the operative CALL should not keep mandating the substitution its own stated falsifier has fired against. C-0714's reformulation is already on the table and unadjudicated: 'discount a D-1 tilt by its measured IMPACT, not its PROVENANCE - provenance needs a cohort field that does not exist, impact is already served.'
